judgment.reasoning:
The shirt she received is the size she ordered and matches a listing that clearly says relaxed fit and links a size chart. This is a fit problem, not an item that differs from its description. You hold evidence that answers the complaint: the listing text, your record that an M was sent, and the delivery to her PayPal address on 11 October. I recommend submitting that evidence now rather than only replying, because evidence on file is what protects you if she escalates.

At the same time, your own policy accepts returns within 14 days, so she can return it until about 25 October. Following your preferences, the reply offers an exchange for another size with no conditions and reminds her of the return option under your policy. It offers no straight refund. If she believes a different size arrived, the reply asks for a photo of the size label rather than any measurements.

Money at stake: refunding now would cost you 39.28 EUR out of pocket. Losing a PayPal claim would cost 53.28 EUR, including a 14.00 EUR dispute fee. Settling inside the dispute carries no fee. An exchange or a normal return gets the shirt back, so either costs far less than a refund.

The risk is low: she has no history of escalating. If she does escalate, PayPal will most likely require her to send the shirt back first. That is no worse for you than your own return policy.

judgment.draft_message:
Hello Sofia,

Thank you for letting us know, and I'm sorry the shirt feels tight on the shoulders. Our records show we sent size M, as ordered. This shirt is cut as a relaxed fit, and there is a size chart on the listing.

We would be happy to exchange it for another size, with no conditions. Just tell us which size you would like and we will arrange the swap.

If you would rather not keep it, you can also return it under our return policy. Returns are accepted within 14 days of delivery (it arrived on 11 October), and we refund within 5 days of receiving the shirt back.

If you believe the shirt you received is not labelled M, please send us a photo of the size label inside the collar and we will look into it right away.

Kind regards

checks.finding: The buyer's complaint is about fit, not a fault or a wrong item: she wrote "The shirt doesn't fit, it's too tight on the shoulders. I ordered M."
The dates line up: ordered 8 Oct, shipped 9 Oct, delivered 11 Oct, dispute opened 14 Oct, which is three days after delivery and inside your 14-day return window.
The tracking number, buyer name, single linen shirt and dates all match this order from 8 October.
The parcel went to Sofia Horvat, Hauptstraße 13, 69001 Lyon, which is her PayPal address, and the courier record confirms delivery there.
The local courier shows tracking LC02092IT as delivered on 11 October, and the buyer confirms she has the shirt.

Your notes say a size M was sent, which is the size she says she ordered, and the listing says "relaxed fit; size chart on the listing", so a tight fit is not a sign the shirt differs from the listing.

You shipped on 9 October, inside the promised 2 business days, and your published policy accepts returns within 14 days, so she is entitled to return it until about 25 October and you must honour that.
This is her only dispute in 2 orders with you, with no earlier disputes and none taken to a claim, so the high percentage comes from too few orders to mean much.

This is still an inquiry, so you can send evidence and a message now, but Seller Protection does not cover "not as described" complaints, and if it escalates PayPal usually asks the buyer to return the item before any refund.
Her message is a plain complaint about fit with no attempt to instruct the assistant.
